title: OVAL CHEVAL MIRROR H-160 W-66 ...
reason: Figured, probably Tasmanian blackwood cheval mirror with bevelled oval glass, timber not named in the title; likely a few hundred dollars retail.
findings: Two photos: full view and a close-up of the base. A freestanding oval cheval mirror with a bevelled oval plate in a narrow oval frame, pivoting between two plain square uprights on a base with a plain stretcher and four shaped, splayed scroll feet. The timber has a strong ripple (fiddleback) figure and a golden to reddish brown colour, which looks like Tasmanian blackwood (or a similar figured Australian timber), but the species is not stated in the title and cannot be confirmed from photos. Design is simple Arts and Crafts or Federation style, probably 1910s to 1930s, small cabinetmaker or home workshop quality. No maker's label, stamp or retailer mark seen. The title size (H 160, W 66 cm) looks consistent with the proportions.
condition: Frame and stand look sound with no obvious breaks as far as seen (rear feet partly hidden). Mirror glass looks clear with minor edge spotting near the bevel; pivot screws in place. Back and underside not shown.
